steps.name: Display
steps.role: Posters, campaign headers, the one line on a slide
steps.sample: The future belongs to all of us.
steps.rules: Two lines maximum. Balance the wraps by hand. Never set in capitals.

steps.name: Headline
steps.role: Section titles, booklet covers, slide openers
steps.sample: Make AI feel like an open door, not a locked lab.
steps.rules: Deep Ink. Optical kerning on. Leave at least 32px of air above it.

steps.name: Title
steps.role: Card titles, question headings, workshop agenda items
steps.sample: What will I actually learn on Saturday?
steps.rules: Use sentence case. A title that needs a colon is usually two titles.

steps.name: Subhead
steps.sample: Free workshops in your neighbourhood, taught in your language.
steps.rules: One sentence. If it runs past two lines it belongs in body copy.

steps.name: Body
steps.sample: Artificial intelligence should be as ordinary and dependable as electricity. You do not need a computer science degree to use it to run a market stall, protect a crop from drought, or help a child with homework.
steps.rules: Atkinson Hyperlegible. 60–70 characters a line. Never justify. Never below 17px on screen or 11pt in print.

steps.name: Small
steps.role: Form help text, footnotes, table cells
steps.sample: Bring a friend. We provide the tablets, the notebooks and the tea.
steps.rules: The smallest size any sentence may be set in.

steps.name: Caption
steps.role: Photo credits, timestamps, table headers, chapter tags
steps.sample: Kibera Community Centre · Nairobi Chapter · 14 March 2026
steps.rules: Separate with middots. Never put it in a pill. Never go below 14px — v1 allowed 13px, which fails for low-vision readers.
